title: Choose Sam's first viewport
question: All three use the same Route Map design language. Choose the composition to carry into the build, or add a note to combine specific parts.

options.label: Route Map
options.lineage: Transit operations diagrams + editorial case files
options.thesis: The promise and the working method share the first viewport at equal weight.
options.viewport: Large statement left, truthful route diagram right, selected work entering below.
options.risk: The method diagram can compete with the work if it becomes too detailed.

options.label: Instrument Board
options.thesis: The first viewport behaves like one live evidence table instead of a hero and cards.
options.viewport: Full-width statement above project routes, with the Workbench preview docked at right.
options.risk: Its density is powerful on desktop but needs disciplined mobile re-composition.

options.label: Quiet Junction
options.thesis: A memorable statement owns the room while the Workbench quietly signals a second world.
options.viewport: Monumental statement, tiny identity metadata, live Workbench aperture, work route at the bottom.
options.risk: The sparse front door must still surface enough proof for time-poor clients.
